<div id="S4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><em id="S4.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">LEASH</em> consistently improves task success over standalone weak-agent execution across all four backbones (Table <a href="#S4.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 4.2 Task Success and Inference Cost ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>). At closely matched escalation rates, it also outperforms random task escalation by 6.55–11.94 percentage points, showing that the training-free uncertainty signal provides useful information for selective weak-to-strong escalation rather than merely increasing access to the strong executor. With Qwen3.5-35B-A3B <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Qwen Team, 2026a</a>)</cite> as the backbone, <em id="S4.SS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">LEASH</em> achieves 73.66% task success while escalating 64.1% of tasks, compared with 72.90% for always-on Opus <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Anthropic, 2026b</a>)</cite>. Besides, its estimated inference cost is
$0.4117 per task, 19.2% lower than the $0.5094 cost of always-on Opus. The benefit also persists at lower escalation rates:
<em id="S4.SS2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">LEASH</em> improves Nemotron-3 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">Deshmukh et al., 2026</a>)</cite> from 45.04% to 66.03% success while escalating 43.1% of tasks, and EvoCUA-8B <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xue et al., 2026</a>)</cite> from 42.37% to 67.18% while escalating 45.4%. This suggests that <em id="S4.SS2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">LEASH</em> can substantially improve overall performance while limiting reliance on the strong executor, yielding a favorable accuracy–cost trade-off across diverse backbones.
The gains are also consistent across weak agents with substantially different standalone capabilities.
Moreover, all four <em id="S4.SS2.p1.1.5" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">LEASH</em> configurations outperform the always-on Sonnet, and three of them do so at lower estimated inference cost. That is, for most backbones, selective escalation to a frontier model is both more accurate and cheaper than running a mid-tier model on every task.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We also compare against StepWise <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wei et al., 2026</a>)</cite> and Progress Advantage <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Oh et al., 2026a</a>)</cite> in Table <a href="#S4.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 4.2 Task Success and Inference Cost ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>. We reproduce StepWise using its released monitor, and for Progress Advantage, we use EvoCUA-8B and Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct as the final and reference policy, respectively, and use its turn-level mean aggregate advantage as negative uncertainty. Both methods use Opus 5 as the strong executor and the same cost accounting as <em id="S4.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">LEASH</em>. We see that <em id="S4.SS2.p2.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">LEASH</em> outperforms other methods with a higher success rate at a comparable escalation rate.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.3 </span>Uncertainty Estimation</h3>

<figure id="S4.T3" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S4.T3.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 3</span>: </span><span id="S4.T3.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">AUROC of uncertainty estimators. For the probability-based column, we report the best-performing uncertainty statistic in each setting. Initial and runtime AUROC use task outcomes and Manager-assigned subgoal outcomes, respectively.
</span></figcaption>
<table id="S4.T3.5" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">
<thead class="ltx_thead">
<tr id="S4.T3.5.1" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="S4.T3.5.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_th_row ltx_border_tt" style="padding:0.35pt 4.0pt;"><span id="S4.T3.5.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Stage</span></th>
<th id="S4.T3.5.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_th_row ltx_border_tt" style="padding:0.35pt 4.0pt;"><span id="S4.T3.5.1.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Backbone</span></th>
<th id="S4.T3.5.1.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt" style="padding:0.35pt 4.0pt;"><span id="S4.T3.5.1.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Probability-based</span></th>
<th id="S4.T3.5.1.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt" style="padding:0.35pt 4.0pt;"><span id="S4.T3.5.1.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Euclidean</span></th>
<th id="S4.T3.5.1.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt" style="padding:0.35pt 4.0pt;"><span id="S4.T3.5.1.5.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">kNN</span></th>
<th id="S4.T3.5.1.6" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_right ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt" style="padding:0.35pt 4.0pt;"><span id="S4.T3.5.1.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Pooled LDA (Ours)</span></th></tr>

<td id="S4.T3.5.5.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_bb" style="padding:0.35pt 4.0pt;"><span id="S4.T3.5.5.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">0.564</span></td>

<td id="S4.T3.5.5.6" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_right ltx_border_bb" style="padding:0.35pt 4.0pt;"><span id="S4.T3.5.5.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">0.575</span></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</figure>
<div id="S4.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We compare output probability-based uncertainty estimates with three representation-based alternatives: Euclidean distance to class centroids, kNN over reference representations, and our pooled LDA using covariance-aware Mahalanobis distance.
The probability-based baseline considers several uncertainty metrics, including negative log-probability, chosen-token probability, predictive entropy, and nucleus-set size under different aggregation schemes <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib65" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gupta et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, and reports the strongest one in each setting.
As shown in Table <a href="#S4.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ 4.3 Uncertainty Estimation ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>, the effectiveness of each uncertainty estimator (i.e., how well it predicts task or sub-goal failure) varies across both backbones and execution stages.
At the initial query-based uncertainty estimation stage, pooled LDA performs best for Nemotron, whereas probability-based baseline is stronger for Qwen3.8-27B. At the runtime step-wise estimation stage, our pooled LDA score achieves the highest AUROC for both backbones, although the overall effectiveness remains moderate.
Overall, these results suggest that representation-based uncertainty can provide a training-free signal for runtime monitoring, particularly highlighting the effectiveness of our LDA-based estimation, while its effectiveness remains dependent on the backbone and execution stage. Meanwhile, the uncertainty estimator is modular in <em id="S4.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">LEASH</em>, allowing alternative, better uncertainty signals to be substituted without changing the escalation workflow depending on available resources or data <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib57" title="" class="ltx_ref">Park et al., 2026b</a>; <a href="#bib.bib58" title="" class="ltx_ref">Park et al., 2026a</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
</section>

<section id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Component-wise ablation.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">As shown in Table <a href="#S4.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ 4.4 Ablation Study ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>, the largest gain comes from enabling uncertainty-guided escalation: task success increases from 41.15% with the Manager to 67.94%, at a higher inference cost. Adding Shadow monitoring and checkpoint intervention further improves success to 73.66% with only a small additional cost, revealing an isolated effectiveness of the post-handoff intervention. Additional backbone ablations are provided in Appendix <a href="#A2.SS3" title="B.3 Additional Component Ablations ‣ Appendix B Additional Experimental Results ‣ LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.3</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">What does Shadow oversight detect?</h4>

<div id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We further examine the tasks on which post-handoff monitoring fires in Table <a href="#S4.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ What does Shadow oversight detect? ‣ 4.4 Ablation Study ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>.
Shadow observer triggers concentrate on particularly difficult trajectories: always-on Opus succeeds on only 51.6% of triggered tasks, compared with 74.5% of escalated tasks without a trigger. On the triggered subset, the Shadow-enabled policy achieves 64.5% success, compared with 48.4% without Shadow. These suggest that the Shadow observer identifies cases where difficulty persists even after escalation, as we expected.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.T5" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S4.T5.7" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 5</span>: </span><span id="S4.T5.8" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Subset analysis of post-handoff Shadow monitoring with Qwen3.5-35B-A3B. <em id="S4.T5.8.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Both escalated</em> contains tasks handed off by both Shadow and No-Shadow policies. <em id="S4.T5.8.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Shadow triggered</em> contains tasks with at least one checkpoint trigger, while <em id="S4.T5.8.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Escalated, not triggered</em> contains escalated tasks without a trigger. <em id="S4.T5.8.4" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Opus only</em> reports always-on Opus accuracy on the same task IDs.</span></figcaption>
<table id="S4.T5.9" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">
<thead class="ltx_thead">

<section id="S4.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.5 </span>Sensitivity Analysis</h3>

<section id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Which tasks to escalate.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We first examine whether uncertainty helps identify which tasks should receive strong-model assistance. Figure <a href="#S4.F5" title="Figure 5 ‣ Which tasks to escalate. ‣ 4.5 Sensitivity Analysis ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> varies the escalation budget and compares <em id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">LEASH</em> with random task-level routing at matched escalation rates.
The random baseline is evaluated at the same operating points, shown by the hollow markers; its near-linear trend follows from uniformly allocating a fixed fraction of tasks to the strong agent. Across varying escalation rates, <em id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">LEASH</em> consistently achieves higher task success, indicating that its gains come from selectively allocating strong-model computation to more informative tasks rather than simply increasing strong-model usage.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.F5" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2">
<figure id="S4.F5.fig1" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_minipage ltx_align_center ltx_align_top" style="width:165.6pt;"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2610.22280v1/ratecurve2.svg" id="S4.F5.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:229/136;" width="229" height="136"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S4.F5.fig1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 4</span>: </span><span id="S4.F5.fig1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Sensitivity to escalation rate on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B. Hollow markers denote the random-routing operating points, each estimated over 4,000 random task allocations.</span></figcaption>
</figure></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2">
<figure id="S4.F5.fig2" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_minipage ltx_align_center ltx_align_top" style="width:165.6pt;"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2610.22280v1/timing3.svg" id="S4.F5.g2" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:229/130;" width="229" height="130"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S4.F5.fig2.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 5</span>: </span><span id="S4.F5.fig2.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Effect of escalation timing on escalation-prone tasks.
<em id="S4.F5.fig2.3.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">LEASH</em> achieves higher success at lower estimated cost than shuffled runtime escalation and always-on Opus.</span></figcaption>
</figure></div></div>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">When to escalate.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We next examine whether the timing of handoff matters once a task is likely to require escalation. We focus on an escalation-prone subset consisting of the tasks most frequently escalated by <em id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">LEASH</em> and compare <em id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">LEASH</em> with a shuffled-timing baseline. As shown in Figure <a href="#S4.F5" title="Figure 5 ‣ Which tasks to escalate. ‣ 4.5 Sensitivity Analysis ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>, <em id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">LEASH</em> achieves 64.6% task success at $0.67 per task, compared with 60.4% at $0.79 under shuffled timing. This 4.2-point improvement, together with 15% lower cost, suggests that effective weak-to-strong escalation depends not only on selecting the right tasks, but also on transferring control at the right point during execution.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Reference bank size.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We examine the effect of reference bank size on initial-stage uncertainty estimation. As shown in Table <a href="#S4.T6" title="Table 6 ‣ Reference bank size. ‣ 4.5 Sensitivity Analysis ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>, increasing the bank size from 40 to 99 improves AUROC from 0.701 to 0.770 for Qwen3.5-35B-A3B and from 0.633 to 0.696 for EvoCUA-8B, highlighting its compatibility for recursively self-improving system <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yin et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ouyang et al., 2026</a>; <a href="#bib.bib56" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lee et al., 2026</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.T6" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S4.T6.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 6</span>: </span><span id="S4.T6.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Sensitivity to reference bank size. <section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Theoretical Analysis</h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Section <a href="#S3" title="3 Method ‣ LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> introduced the distance-based uncertainty score in Eq. (<a href="#S3.E3" title="In Uncertainty score. ‣ 3.2 Reference-Based Latent Uncertainty Estimation ‣ 3 Method ‣ LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>), and Section <a href="#S4" title="4 Experiments ‣ LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> showed that escalating on that score outperforms random escalation at matched rates. In this section, we now explain the empirical success of our uncertainty-based escalation through a simple probabilistic analysis.
To keep the analysis simple, we consider a single decision per task: each task is either handed to the strong agent before execution begins (<math id="S5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{\mathrm{esc}}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>esc</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{\mathrm{esc}}=0</annotation></semantics></math>) or never handed off (<math id="S5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{\mathrm{esc}}=T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>esc</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{\mathrm{esc}}=T</annotation></semantics></math>). This isolates the initial gate <math id="S5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> of <em id="S5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">LEASH</em> (Section <a href="#S3.SS3" title="3.3 Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation ‣ 3 Method ‣ LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3</span></a>), with no runtime escalation afterward. We also assume the budget in Eq. (<a href="#S3.E1" title="In 3.1 Problem Formulation ‣ 3 Method ‣ LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>) is used exactly, so a fixed fraction <math id="S5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> of tasks is escalated, which is what our quantile thresholds target.
Let <math id="S5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math> be the standardized query representation, <math id="S5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y\in\{\textup{{Pass}},\textup{{Fail}}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">Pass</mtext><mo>,</mo><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">Fail</mtext></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y\in\{\textup{{Pass}},\textup{{Fail}}\}</annotation></semantics></math> the outcome if the weak agent completes the task without escalation, and <math id="S5.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{\mathrm{w}}(z)=\Pr(Y=\textup{{Pass}}\mid z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>w</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>Pr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo>=</mo><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">Pass</mtext></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{\mathrm{w}}(z)=\Pr(Y=\textup{{Pass}}\mid z)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S5.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{\mathrm{s}}(z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{\mathrm{s}}(z)</annotation></semantics></math> the success probabilities when the weak agent and the strong agent, respectively, completes the task. We analyze <math id="S5.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u(z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u(z)</annotation></semantics></math>, the population version of our initial score <math id="S5.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u_{q}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u_{q}</annotation></semantics></math> in Eq. (<a href="#S3.E3" title="In Uncertainty score. ‣ 3.2 Reference-Based Latent Uncertainty Estimation ‣ 3 Method ‣ LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>), computed with the true class means and covariance instead of their estimates.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmproposition1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_proposition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmproposition1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition 1</span></span><span id="Thmproposition1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Optimality of <em id="Thmproposition1.4" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">LEASH</em>’s initial gate at a fixed escalation rate)<span id="Thmproposition1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmproposition1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmproposition1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmproposition1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Suppose <math id="Thmproposition1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z\mid Y=y\sim\mathcal{N}(\mu_{y},\Sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo fence="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>y</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z\mid Y=y\sim\mathcal{N}(\mu_{y},\Sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> with shared covariance <math id="Thmproposition1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma\succ 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo>≻</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma\succ 0</annotation></semantics></math> and distinct means, and both outcomes occur with positive probability. Let the initial gate escalate a task when <math id="Thmproposition1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u(z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u(z)</annotation></semantics></math> exceeds the threshold that escalates a fraction <math id="Thmproposition1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> of tasks. Among all escalation rules based on <math id="Thmproposition1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math> with the same rate <math id="Thmproposition1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math>:</span></p>
<ol id="S5.I1" class="ltx_enumerate ltx_leftmargin_flush">
<li id="S5.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">(i)</span> 
<div id="S5.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">the gate hands off the largest fraction of the tasks the weak agent would fail, i.e., it maximizes </span><math id="S5.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Pr(\text{escalated}\mid Y=\textup{{Fail}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Pr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic">escalated</mtext><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo>=</mo><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">Fail</mtext></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Pr(\text{escalated}\mid Y=\textup{{Fail}})</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S5.I1.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">;</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">(ii)</span> 
<div id="S5.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">if the escalation gain </span><math id="S5.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta(z)=q_{\mathrm{s}}(z)-q_{\mathrm{w}}(z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>w</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta(z)=q_{\mathrm{s}}(z)-q_{\mathrm{w}}(z)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S5.I1.i2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> is a nondecreasing function of </span><math id="S5.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u(z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u(z)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S5.I1.i2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">, and when </span><math id="S5.I1.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{\mathrm{s}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{\mathrm{s}}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S5.I1.i2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> is constant, the gate also maximizes task success rate.</span></p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
</div>
<section id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Proof sketch.</h4>

<div id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Under this model, our score equals (up to an additive constant) twice the log-odds that the weak agent fails (Lemma <a href="#Thmlemma1" title="Lemma 1 (Distance score as failure log-odds). ‣ Relative distance and the fitted score. ‣ A.1 Routing Details, Analyses and Proofs ‣ Appendix A Method and Formulation Details ‣ LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> in Appendix <a href="#A1.SS1" title="A.1 Routing Details, Analyses and Proofs ‣ Appendix A Method and Formulation Details ‣ LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.1</span></a>), which recalls the classical linear discriminant analysis identity <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib59" title="" class="ltx_ref">Fisher, 1936</a>)</cite>. Escalating the highest-scoring tasks thus escalates the tasks most likely to fail, and a Neyman–Pearson exchange argument <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">Neyman and Pearson, 1933</a>)</cite> shows that no other rule at the same rate catches more failures; (ii) follows by the same argument applied to <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Implication.</h4>

<div id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Proposition <a href="#Thmproposition1" title="Proposition 1 (Optimality of LEASH’s initial gate at a fixed escalation rate). ‣ 5 Theoretical Analysis ‣ LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> (i) says that, at any escalation budget, no escalation rule based on the query representation <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math> captures more of the weak agent’s failures than the initial gate of <em id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">LEASH</em>. For example, random escalation with budget <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> hands off only a fraction <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> of these failures, whereas our gate hands off strictly more. Moreover, (ii) shows that our gate spends the strong-agent budget where it pays off most <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib63" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jitkrittum et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, so catching more of the weak agent’s failures directly turns into higher overall task success. Meanwhile, the analysis covers only the initial gate; analyzing the runtime gate would require an optimal-stopping formulation, which we leave to future work.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">6 </span>Conclusion</h2>

<div id="S6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We introduced <em id="S6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">weak to strong escalation</em> as a general inference paradigm for adaptive agent systems, in which inexpensive weak models handle routine execution and stronger models are invoked selectively when additional capability is needed. Under this paradigm, we proposed <em id="S6.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">LEASH</em>, a training-free, uncertainty-aware framework that supports initial routing, runtime escalation, and continued post-handoff oversight. Our results suggest that a shared latent uncertainty signal can support both selective escalation and post-handoff oversight, providing a practical mechanism for dynamically allocating model capability while retaining continued control over strong-agent execution.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="Sx1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section">Limitations</h2>

<div id="Sx1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Our current evaluation is limited to computer-use agents on OSWorld, so the generality of weak-to-strong escalation beyond this domain remains to be validated. In addition, our uncertainty score estimates weak-agent failure risk rather than the expected benefit of escalation; Proposition <a href="#Thmproposition1" title="Proposition 1 (Optimality of LEASH’s initial gate at a fixed escalation rate). ‣ 5 Theoretical Analysis ‣ LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> requires a condition that the escalation gain be nondecreasing in the score, which may fail when both weak and strong agents struggle on the same task.
Finally, post-handoff Shadow monitoring operates under a distribution shift from weak-agent trajectories, and its intervention effect is not causally isolated in our current evaluation.</p>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>

<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>Method and Formulation Details</h2>

<section id="A1.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.1 </span>Routing Details, Analyses and Proofs</h3>

<section id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Setup and notation.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Section <a href="#S5" title="5 Theoretical Analysis ‣ LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> analyzes a single routing decision made before execution, i.e., Eq. (<a href="#S3.E1" title="In 3.1 Problem Formulation ‣ 3 Method ‣ LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>) restricted to <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{\mathrm{esc}}\in\{0,T\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>esc</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{\mathrm{esc}}\in\{0,T\}</annotation></semantics></math>. We keep both agents fixed and compare only routing rules. Let <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{\mathrm{w}}(z)=\Pr(Y=\textup{{Pass}}\mid z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>w</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>Pr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo>=</mo><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">Pass</mtext></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{\mathrm{w}}(z)=\Pr(Y=\textup{{Pass}}\mid z)</annotation></semantics></math> be the success probability if the weak agent completes the task without escalation, and <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{\mathrm{s}}(z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{\mathrm{s}}(z)</annotation></semantics></math> the success probability if the strong agent completes it. A routing rule <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi(z)\in[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi(z)\in[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math> escalates a task with probability <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi(z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi(z)</annotation></semantics></math>, using only <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math>, i.e., without knowing whether the task would actually succeed. Defining <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta(z)=q_{\mathrm{s}}(z)-q_{\mathrm{w}}(z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>w</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta(z)=q_{\mathrm{s}}(z)-q_{\mathrm{w}}(z)</annotation></semantics></math> for the success gain from escalation, the overall success rate decomposes as</p>
<table id="A1.E5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J(\phi)=\mathbb{E}\bigl[(1-\phi(z))q_{\mathrm{w}}(z)+\phi(z)q_{\mathrm{s}}(z)\bigr]=\mathbb{E}[q_{\mathrm{w}}(z)]+\mathbb{E}[\phi(z)\Delta(z)]." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>w</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>w</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J(\phi)=\mathbb{E}\bigl[(1-\phi(z))q_{\mathrm{w}}(z)+\phi(z)q_{\mathrm{s}}(z)\bigr]=\mathbb{E}[q_{\mathrm{w}}(z)]+\mathbb{E}[\phi(z)\Delta(z)].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(5)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">For the proofs, we will use the threshold-exchange argument underlying the Neyman–Pearson lemma <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">Neyman and Pearson, 1933</a>)</cite>, with a constraint on the marginal escalation rate rather than a class-conditional false-positive rate.</p>
</div>
</section>

<p id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.3" class="ltx_p">Since the shared quadratic term cancels, <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u_{c}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u_{c}</annotation></semantics></math> measures displacement along <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma_{c,\lambda}^{-1}(\mu_{c,\textup{{Fail}}}-\mu_{c,\textup{{Pass}}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>λ</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>μ</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">Fail</mtext></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>μ</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">Pass</mtext></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma_{c,\lambda}^{-1}(\mu_{c,\textup{{Fail}}}-\mu_{c,\textup{{Pass}}})</annotation></semantics></math>. Note that this identity holds for the fitted score without any distributional assumption, and the Gaussian model is needed only for the population likelihood-ratio interpretation below.</p>

<div id="Thmlemma1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmlemma1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 1</span></span><span id="Thmlemma1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Distance score as failure log-odds)<span id="Thmlemma1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmlemma1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmlemma1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmlemma1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Under the Gaussian model of Proposition <a href="#Thmproposition1" title="Proposition 1 (Optimality of LEASH’s initial gate at a fixed escalation rate). ‣ 5 Theoretical Analysis ‣ LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>, let <math id="Thmlemma1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{y}=\Pr(Y=y)&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>y</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>Pr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{y}=\Pr(Y=y)&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> be the class priors and <math id="Thmlemma1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{y}^{2}(z)=(z-\mu_{y})^{\top}\Sigma^{-1}(z-\mu_{y})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>y</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>y</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{y}^{2}(z)=(z-\mu_{y})^{\top}\Sigma^{-1}(z-\mu_{y})</annotation></semantics></math>, so that <math id="Thmlemma1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u(z)=d_{\textup{{Pass}}}^{2}(z)-d_{\textup{{Fail}}}^{2}(z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>d</mi><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">Pass</mtext><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>d</mi><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">Fail</mtext><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u(z)=d_{\textup{{Pass}}}^{2}(z)-d_{\textup{{Fail}}}^{2}(z)</annotation></semantics></math>. Then the weak agent’s failure risk <math id="Thmlemma1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta(z)=\Pr(Y=\textup{{Fail}}\mid z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>Pr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo>=</mo><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">Fail</mtext></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta(z)=\Pr(Y=\textup{{Fail}}\mid z)</annotation></semantics></math> satisfies</span></p>
<table id="A1.E7" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\log\frac{\eta(z)}{1-\eta(z)}=\tfrac{1}{2}u(z)+\log\frac{\pi_{\textup{{Fail}}}}{\pi_{\textup{{Pass}}}}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="false"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>u</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mfrac><msub><mi>π</mi><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">Fail</mtext></msub><msub><mi>π</mi><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">Pass</mtext></msub></mfrac></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log\frac{\eta(z)}{1-\eta(z)}=\tfrac{1}{2}u(z)+\log\frac{\pi_{\textup{{Fail}}}}{\pi_{\textup{{Pass}}}},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(7)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="Thmlemma1.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmlemma1.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">so <math id="Thmlemma1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>η</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta</annotation></semantics></math> is strictly increasing in <math id="Thmlemma1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>u</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>

</div>
<div id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.1" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof of Lemma <a href="#Thmlemma1" title="Lemma 1 (Distance score as failure log-odds). ‣ Relative distance and the fitted score. ‣ A.1 Routing Details, Analyses and Proofs ‣ Appendix A Method and Formulation Details ‣ LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>.</h6>
<div id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">Let <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{y}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>y</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{y}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the class-conditional Gaussian density. The shared covariance cancels the density normalizer terms, resulting in</span></p>
<table id="A1.Ex1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.Ex1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\log\frac{f_{\textup{{Fail}}}(z)}{f_{\textup{{Pass}}}(z)}=-\tfrac{1}{2}d_{\textup{{Fail}}}^{2}(z)+\tfrac{1}{2}d_{\textup{{Pass}}}^{2}(z)=\tfrac{1}{2}u(z)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">Fail</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">Pass</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="false"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>d</mi><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">Fail</mtext><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="false"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>d</mi><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">Pass</mtext><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="false"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>u</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log\frac{f_{\textup{{Fail}}}(z)}{f_{\textup{{Pass}}}(z)}=-\tfrac{1}{2}d_{\textup{{Fail}}}^{2}(z)+\tfrac{1}{2}d_{\textup{{Pass}}}^{2}(z)=\tfrac{1}{2}u(z).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.2.1" class="ltx_text">By Bayes’ rule, <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\log\{\eta/(1-\eta)\}=\log(f_{\textup{{Fail}}}/f_{\textup{{Pass}}})+\log(\pi_{\textup{{Fail}}}/\pi_{\textup{{Pass}}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>η</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">Fail</mtext></msub><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">Pass</mtext></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">Fail</mtext></msub><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">Pass</mtext></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log\{\eta/(1-\eta)\}=\log(f_{\textup{{Fail}}}/f_{\textup{{Pass}}})+\log(\pi_{\textup{{Fail}}}/\pi_{\textup{{Pass}}})</annotation></semantics></math>, which gives Eq. (<a href="#A1.E7" title="In Lemma 1 (Distance score as failure log-odds). ‣ Relative distance and the fitted score. ‣ A.1 Routing Details, Analyses and Proofs ‣ Appendix A Method and Formulation Details ‣ LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>). The log-odds are strictly increasing in <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>η</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>η</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta</annotation></semantics></math> is a strictly increasing function of <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>u</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof of Proposition <a href="#Thmproposition1" title="Proposition 1 (Optimality of LEASH’s initial gate at a fixed escalation rate). ‣ 5 Theoretical Analysis ‣ LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>.</h6>
<div id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text">Denote <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta=\mu_{\textup{{Fail}}}-\mu_{\textup{{Pass}}}\neq 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>μ</mi><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">Fail</mtext></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>μ</mi><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">Pass</mtext></msub></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta=\mu_{\textup{{Fail}}}-\mu_{\textup{{Pass}}}\neq 0</annotation></semantics></math>. By the expansion in Eq. (<a href="#A1.E6" title="In Relative distance and the fitted score. ‣ A.1 Routing Details, Analyses and Proofs ‣ Appendix A Method and Formulation Details ‣ LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>), <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u(z)=2\delta^{\top}\Sigma^{-1}z+b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>δ</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u(z)=2\delta^{\top}\Sigma^{-1}z+b</annotation></semantics></math> for a constant <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>b</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math>, so within each class <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>u</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u</annotation></semantics></math> is Gaussian with variance <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4\delta^{\top}\Sigma^{-1}\delta&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>δ</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4\delta^{\top}\Sigma^{-1}\delta&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>. The distribution of <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>u</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u</annotation></semantics></math> is therefore a mixture of two Gaussians with positive variance, which has a positive density on <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ℝ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}</annotation></semantics></math>, so a unique <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{p}</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Pr(u&gt;\tau_{p})=p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>Pr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Pr(u&gt;\tau_{p})=p</annotation></semantics></math> exists. The initial gate at rate <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> is <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p3.m11" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\phi^{\star}(z)=\mathbb{I}\{u(z)&gt;\tau_{p}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>𝕀</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>u</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi^{\star}(z)=\mathbb{I}\{u(z)&gt;\tau_{p}\}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><em id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">(i)</em><span id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.1.2" class="ltx_text"> Let <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>η</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta_{p}</annotation></semantics></math> be the failure risk at <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u=\tau_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u=\tau_{p}</annotation></semantics></math>, and let <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϕ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi</annotation></semantics></math> be any rule with <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}[\phi]=p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[\phi]=p</annotation></semantics></math>. Since <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϕ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi</annotation></semantics></math> uses only <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math>, a task with representation <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math> is escalated with probability <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi(z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi(z)</annotation></semantics></math> regardless of whether it would fail, so <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Pr(\text{escalated},Y=\textup{{Fail}})=\mathbb{E}[\phi\eta]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>Pr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mtext>escalated</mtext><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo>=</mo><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">Fail</mtext></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>η</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Pr(\text{escalated},Y=\textup{{Fail}})=\mathbb{E}[\phi\eta]</annotation></semantics></math>. Because both rules escalate the same fraction of tasks, <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}[\phi^{\star}-\phi]=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mo>−</mo><mi>ϕ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[\phi^{\star}-\phi]=0</annotation></semantics></math>, and we may subtract the constant <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>η</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta_{p}</annotation></semantics></math>:</span></p>
<table id="A1.Ex2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.Ex2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}[\phi^{\star}\eta]-\mathbb{E}[\phi\eta]=\mathbb{E}\bigl[(\phi^{\star}-\phi)(\eta-\eta_{p})\bigr]\geq 0." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>η</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>η</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mo>−</mo><mi>ϕ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>η</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[\phi^{\star}\eta]-\mathbb{E}[\phi\eta]=\mathbb{E}\bigl[(\phi^{\star}-\phi)(\eta-\eta_{p})\bigr]\geq 0.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.2.1" class="ltx_text">By Lemma <a href="#Thmlemma1" title="Lemma 1 (Distance score as failure log-odds). ‣ Relative distance and the fitted score. ‣ A.1 Routing Details, Analyses and Proofs ‣ Appendix A Method and Formulation Details ‣ LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>, <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta\geq\eta_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo>≥</mo><msub><mi>η</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta\geq\eta_{p}</annotation></semantics></math> wherever <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi^{\star}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi^{\star}=1</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta\leq\eta_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo>≤</mo><msub><mi>η</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta\leq\eta_{p}</annotation></semantics></math> wherever <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi^{\star}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi^{\star}=0</annotation></semantics></math>.
For random escalation, <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi\equiv p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>≡</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi\equiv p</annotation></semantics></math>, the integrand <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\phi^{\star}-p)(\eta-\eta_{p})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mo>−</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>η</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\phi^{\star}-p)(\eta-\eta_{p})</annotation></semantics></math> is strictly positive whenever <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u\neq\tau_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>≠</mo><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u\neq\tau_{p}</annotation></semantics></math>, because <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>η</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta</annotation></semantics></math> is strictly increasing in <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>u</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u</annotation></semantics></math>. Therefore, the inequality is strict, and while random escalation hands off exactly a fraction <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> of the failures, <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> hands off strictly more.
Dividing by <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{\textup{{Fail}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>π</mi><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">Fail</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{\textup{{Fail}}}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> also maximizes <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m25" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Pr(\text{escalated}\mid Y=\textup{{Fail}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Pr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mtext>escalated</mtext><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo>=</mo><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">Fail</mtext></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Pr(\text{escalated}\mid Y=\textup{{Fail}})</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><em id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">(ii)</em><span id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.1.2" class="ltx_text"> Since <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y</annotation></semantics></math> is the weak agent’s outcome, <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{\mathrm{w}}(z)=1-\eta(z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>w</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{\mathrm{w}}(z)=1-\eta(z)</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta(z)=q_{\mathrm{s}}(z)-1+\eta(z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta(z)=q_{\mathrm{s}}(z)-1+\eta(z)</annotation></semantics></math>. Suppose <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta(z)=g(u(z))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta(z)=g(u(z))</annotation></semantics></math> for a nondecreasing <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math>, and let <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{p}=g(\tau_{p})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{p}=g(\tau_{p})</annotation></semantics></math>. By Eq. (<a href="#A1.E5" title="In Setup and notation. ‣ A.1 Routing Details, Analyses and Proofs ‣ Appendix A Method and Formulation Details ‣ LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>) and the same subtraction,</span></p>
<table id="A1.Ex3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.Ex3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J(\phi^{\star})-J(\phi)=\mathbb{E}\bigl[(\phi^{\star}-\phi)\Delta\bigr]=\mathbb{E}\bigl[(\phi^{\star}-\phi)(\Delta-\Delta_{p})\bigr]\geq 0," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mo>−</mo><mi>ϕ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mo>−</mo><mi>ϕ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J(\phi^{\star})-J(\phi)=\mathbb{E}\bigl[(\phi^{\star}-\phi)\Delta\bigr]=\mathbb{E}\bigl[(\phi^{\star}-\phi)(\Delta-\Delta_{p})\bigr]\geq 0,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.2.1" class="ltx_text">since <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta\geq\Delta_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>≥</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta\geq\Delta_{p}</annotation></semantics></math> wherever <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi^{\star}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi^{\star}=1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta\leq\Delta_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>≤</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta\leq\Delta_{p}</annotation></semantics></math> wherever <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi^{\star}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi^{\star}=0</annotation></semantics></math>. If <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{\mathrm{s}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{\mathrm{s}}</annotation></semantics></math> is constant, <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> is strictly increasing, so the condition holds.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.2 </span>Representations and Estimator Fitting</h3>

<section id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Layer and token.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We use the last transformer layer of each weak backbone (Table <a href="#A1.T7" title="Table 7 ‣ Layer and token. ‣ A.2 Representations and Estimator Fitting ‣ Appendix A Method and Formulation Details ‣ LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>). For the runtime channel, <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> is the hidden state at the last generated token of the action; we apply no pooling within a step and no temporal window across steps, so every step contributes one representation. For the initial channel, we reissue the task’s first request with a one-token generation limit and read the hidden state at the final prompt position, obtained during prefill.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A1.T7" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="A1.T7.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 7</span>: </span><span id="A1.T7.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Hidden layer used for each weak backbone (0-indexed layer / number of layers).</span></figcaption>
