</tbody>
</table>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Standardization and covariance.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Standardization uses the feature-wise mean and standard deviation of the channel’s bank, pooled across both classes. The class centroids are computed in the standardized space, and <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widehat{\Sigma}_{c}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>c</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widehat{\Sigma}_{c}</annotation></semantics></math> is the pooled within-class scatter normalized by <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n-2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n-2</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> is the number of representations in the bank.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Selecting the ridge parameter.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We select <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{c}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{c}</annotation></semantics></math> from a grid spanning <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{-2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{-2}</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{3}</annotation></semantics></math> by task-grouped 10-fold cross-validated AUROC, separately for each backbone and channel. Grouping by task is essential: steps from one trajectory share much of their context and, at runtime, their segment label. In a preliminary check, a split that ignored task membership produced a near-perfect AUROC of 0.997, which reflected leakage across steps of the same trajectory rather than genuine discrimination.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.3 </span>Reference Banks and Threshold Calibration</h3>

<section id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Reference banks.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For each backbone, we construct a small held-out set of Manager-guided trajectories collected with escalation disabled and disjoint from the evaluation tasks. From this set, we construct the query and action representation banks: initial representations are labeled by task-level outcomes, while runtime representations inherit the outcomes of their corresponding subgoal segments.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Held-out scoring.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We use the same held-out reference set for both representation-bank construction and threshold calibration. Specifically, we perform task-grouped 10-fold cross-validation, keeping all steps from the same task in one fold. For each fold, an uncertainty estimator is fitted on the other nine folds and used only to score the held-out fold, yielding one out-of-fold score for every reference
task. The fold-specific estimators are used only for calibration and are discarded afterwards.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We then set the escalation thresholds as empirical quantiles of these out-of-fold scores. After calibration, we fit one final estimator per uncertainty channel on all tasks in the same reference set, keep the calibrated thresholds fixed, and use these final estimators to score the evaluation tasks. No evaluation data are used for either estimator fitting or threshold calibration.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Targets and thresholds.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">All four backbones use the same targets, <math id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{q}=0.25" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.25</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{q}=0.25</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{\mathrm{esc}}=0.50" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>esc</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.50</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{\mathrm{esc}}=0.50</annotation></semantics></math>, so that <math id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{a}=(p_{\mathrm{esc}}-p_{q})/(1-p_{q})=1/3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>esc</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>q</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>q</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{a}=(p_{\mathrm{esc}}-p_{q})/(1-p_{q})=1/3</annotation></semantics></math>. The thresholds <math id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{q}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{q}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{a}</annotation></semantics></math> are exact order statistics of the held-out scores in Eq. (<a href="#S3.E4" title="In Calibrating gating threshold to an escalation budget. ‣ 3.3 Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation ‣ 3 Method ‣ LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>). Because the reference set is finite, the achievable rates are discrete, with a resolution of one reference task.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.4 </span>Post-Handoff Oversight</h3>

<section id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Probe schedule and context.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Shadow probes run at the first strong-agent step after handoff and at every third step thereafter. At every strong-agent step, including steps without a probe, the executed action is appended to the weak model’s history in that model’s own action format, so that each probe conditions on the actual trajectory rather than on the pre-handoff context. A probe calls the weak agent’s own action-generation routine, with its usual system prompt, tool schema, and image history, and does not invoke the Manager. The candidate action is logged for analysis but never executed or shown to the strong agent.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Shadow threshold.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{\mathrm{sh}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>sh</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{\mathrm{sh}}</annotation></semantics></math> is the 90th percentile of the pooled per-step runtime scores over the 99-task reference pool, computed separately for each backbone. It is derived directly from the reference pool rather than from the escalation thresholds. For EvoCUA-8B, the in-sample value (<math id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+1.7309" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1.7309</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+1.7309</annotation></semantics></math>) is close to the corresponding out-of-fold value (<math id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+1.7106" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1.7106</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+1.7106</annotation></semantics></math>).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Checkpoint budget.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">At most six checkpoints can fire in an episode. In addition, once two checkpoints have changed the strong agent’s action, further firings are suppressed; checkpoints that leave the action unchanged do not count toward this second limit. Because probes occur every three steps, consecutive checkpoints are at least three steps apart.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Checkpoint mechanics.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">When a checkpoint fires, the strong agent’s conversation is truncated to its length at the start of the current step, which removes the pending action; the neutral checkpoint message in Figure <a href="#A3.F7" title="Figure 7 ‣ Appendix C Prompt Templates ‣ LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> is appended; and the strong agent re-decides the step with a raised reasoning-effort setting. The weak model’s candidate action is deliberately excluded from the checkpoint message, so the strong agent is never steered toward a specific action proposed by the weaker model.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix B </span>Additional Experimental Results</h2>

<section id="A2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.1 </span>Experimental Details</h3>

<section id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Evaluation setting.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate on OSWorld with screenshot observations and a shared budget of 50 actions per task. The lightweight backbones are EvoCUA-8B <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xue et al., 2026</a>)</cite>, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Qwen Team, 2026a</a>)</cite>, Nemotron-3-Nano-Omni (30B-A3B) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">Deshmukh et al., 2026</a>)</cite>, and Qwen3.8-27B <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Qwen Team, 2026b</a>)</cite>. Claude Opus 5 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Anthropic, 2026b</a>)</cite> serves as both the Manager and strong executor, and Claude Sonnet 4.5 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">Anthropic, 2025</a>)</cite> is an additional always-on reference. The always-on references run the strong model alone, without the Manager, so they measure strong-model capability without the Manager or escalation framework.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Configurations and evaluation sets.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><em id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Manager</em> adds subgoal planning and verification; <em id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Escalation</em> further enables initial and runtime handoff; and <em id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">LEASH</em> additionally enables post-handoff Shadow monitoring and corresponding intervention. These configurations are cumulative. Shared results below follow Tables <a href="#S4.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 4.2 Task Success and Inference Cost ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> and <a href="#S4.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ 4.4 Ablation Study ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>. The evaluation task pool contains 262 tasks.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Reference banks and calibration.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We use a held-out reference set that is disjoint from the 262 evaluation tasks. We obtain task-grouped 10-fold out-of-fold scores, keeping all observations from a task in one fold; preprocessing and estimator fitting use only the training folds. Initial scores use final task outcomes and runtime scores use Manager-assigned subgoal outcomes. Thresholds are order statistics of the held-out scores targeting a 25% initial and 50% overall escalation frequency, with runtime calibration based on per-task maximum scores. Refitting slightly changes the score scale, and differences between the reference and evaluation sets can further affect the realized escalation rate; hence the observed rates (43–64%) need not exactly match the calibration targets.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Post-handoff execution.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">After handoff, Shadow probes query the lightweight model every three strong-agent steps. Probe actions are not executed; their hidden representations provide the monitoring scores. Higher scores indicate greater uncertainty and can trigger an intervention that asks the strong agent to reassess its current strategy while retaining control.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Cost estimation.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We estimate inference cost from recorded token usage using OpenRouter reference prices, accounting for cached tokens where applicable. Total cost includes lightweight-agent, Manager, strong-executor, and monitoring calls. For locally served models, we report reference inference-cost estimates rather than measured hardware costs.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.2 </span>Uncertainty Estimation and Reference-Bank Sensitivity</h3>

<section id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Estimator comparison.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We compare pooled LDA with Euclidean distance, kNN, and probability-based baselines. The probability-based baseline considers negative log-probability, chosen-token probability, predictive entropy, and nucleus-set size under several aggregation schemes; we report the strongest statistic in each setting. Performance varies across backbones and execution stages, with pooled LDA providing the strongest overall discrimination in most settings. Runtime AUROC reflects discrimination of Manager-assigned subgoal-segment outcomes rather than individual action correctness.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Reference-bank size.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S4.T6" title="Table 6 ‣ Reference bank size. ‣ 4.5 Sensitivity Analysis ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> reports initial-stage AUROC as the bank is subsampled, it also shows that estimates become more stable as the bank grows: the standard deviation decreases from roughly 0.10 at 40 tasks to about 0.02 at 99 tasks. Because thresholds are quantiles of this same pool, a small bank also gives coarse control of the realized escalation rate.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.3 </span>Additional Component Ablations</h3>

<section id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Initial and runtime escalation.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A2.T8" title="Table 8 ‣ Initial and runtime escalation. ‣ B.3 Additional Component Ablations ‣ Appendix B Additional Experimental Results ‣ LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> compares different gate configurations for Qwen3.5-35B-A3B. Runtime-only escalation achieves higher success than initial-only escalation, at higher cost, indicating that runtime monitoring provides the stronger escalation signal. The complete framework attains the best overall performance, but it also enables Shadow oversight. Its counterpart without Shadow is the <em id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Escalation</em> configuration in Table <a href="#S4.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ 4.4 Ablation Study ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> (67.94% at $0.4050), which falls below runtime-only escalation, so this ablation does not show a benefit from adding the initial gate to the runtime gate in this setting.</p>
</div>

</section>
<section id="A2.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.4 </span>Inference Cost</h3>

<div id="A2.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Runtime uncertainty scoring reuses hidden states from the weak agent’s action generation and therefore requires no additional model call. Initial and Shadow probes require lightweight-model inference, while interventions may incur additional strong-model computation. All such costs are already included in the total workflow cost reported in Table <a href="#S4.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 4.2 Task Success and Inference Cost ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A3" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix C </span>Prompt Templates</h2>

<div id="A3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figures <a href="#A3.F6" title="Figure 6 ‣ Appendix C Prompt Templates ‣ LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> and <a href="#A3.F7" title="Figure 7 ‣ Appendix C Prompt Templates ‣ LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> show the core prompts used for planning, verification, handoff, and checkpoint intervention. The planning prompt is excerpted, with omissions marked by <span id="A3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">[...]</span>; braces denote runtime placeholders in the handoff template. Escalation gates use statistical scores and require no prompt. Shadow candidate actions are neither executed nor shown to the strong agent.</p>
</div>

<span id="A3.F6.pic1.2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.F6.pic1.2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:80%;width:471.0pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A3.F6.pic1.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.F6.pic1.2.1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.F6.pic1.2.1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:17.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.F6.pic1.2.1.1.4" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:454.0pt;">
<span id="A3.F6.pic1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.F6.pic1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">You are a planning agent for a SINGLE computer-use agent operating ONE Ubuntu desktop. You are a regular LLM — you cannot click or type yourself; a downstream agent executes pyautogui actions one step at a time. Your job is to take one desktop task and decompose it into a SHORT, ORDERED list of subgoals the agent completes sequentially, each with a concrete done-criterion that a verifier can confirm from a screenshot.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A3.F6.pic1.2.2" class="ltx_p" style="width:471.0pt;"><span id="A3.F6.pic1.2.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:80%;width:471.0pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A3.F6.pic1.2.2.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:471.0pt;"></span></span></span>

<span id="A3.F6.pic1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.F6.pic1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">[...]</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A3.F6.pic1.2.4" class="ltx_p" style="width:471.0pt;"><span id="A3.F6.pic1.2.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:80%;width:471.0pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A3.F6.pic1.2.4.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:471.0pt;"></span></span></span>
<span id="A3.F6.pic1.2.5" class="ltx_p" style="width:471.0pt;"><span id="A3.F6.pic1.2.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:80%;width:471.0pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A3.F6.pic1.2.5.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:471.0pt;">
<span id="A3.F6.pic1.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.F6.pic1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">## Output format</span>
</span></span></span></span>

<span id="A3.F6.pic2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">## Strict verification (IMPORTANT)</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A3.F6.pic2.2.2" class="ltx_p" style="width:471.0pt;"><span id="A3.F6.pic2.2.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:80%;width:471.0pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A3.F6.pic2.2.2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.F6.pic2.2.2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.F6.pic2.2.2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:17.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.F6.pic2.2.2.1.4" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:454.0pt;">
<span id="A3.F6.pic2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.F6.pic2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">When you choose `advance`, you MUST positively confirm from the CURRENT screenshot that the focus sub-goal’s completion criterion is CONCRETELY and FULLY satisfied by the actual end-state — not merely that the relevant application, window, file, menu, or element is present, open, or focused. If you cannot positively verify the required end-state from what is visibly on screen, do NOT advance — choose `no_change` or `revise` instead. Do not assume an action succeeded just because it was attempted.</span>

<span id="A3.F7.pic1.p13.1" class="ltx_p">The attempts above were made by a weaker agent and did not complete the task. You are taking over. Work from the CURRENT screenshot.</span>

</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span></div><div class="ltx_flex_break"></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="A3.F7.pic2" class="ltx_picture ltx_centering ltx_figure_panel" height="130.4" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 676.77 130.4" width="676.77"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,130.4) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#737373;" fill="#737373" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 4.63 L 0 125.77 C 0 128.33 2.07 130.4 4.63 130.4 L 672.14 130.4 C 674.7 130.4 676.77 128.33 676.77 125.77 L 676.77 4.63 C 676.77 2.07 674.7 0 672.14 0 L 4.63 0 C 2.07 0 0 2.07 0 4.63 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#FBFBFB;" fill="#FBFBFB" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0.69 4.63 L 0.69 108.69 L 676.08 108.69 L 676.08 4.63 C 676.08 2.45 674.32 0.69 672.14 0.69 L 4.63 0.69 C 2.45 0.69 0.69 2.45 0.69 4.63 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 12.5 116.43)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:44.23em;--ltx-fo-height:0.68em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.23em;font-size:10pt;" height="12.45" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 9.34)" width="612.02"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="A3.F7.pic2.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:44.23em;">
<span id="A3.F7.pic2.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.F7.pic2.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#FFFFFF;">Post-handoff checkpoint (intervention message)</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 12.5 11.03)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:55.41em;--ltx-fo-height:6.49em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.18em;font-size:10pt;" height="92.25" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 89.79)" width="766.72"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="A3.F7.pic2.2" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:55.41em;">
<span id="A3.F7.pic2.2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.F7.pic2.2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:80%;width:471.0pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A3.F7.pic2.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:471.0pt;">
<span id="A3.F7.pic2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.F7.pic2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">CHECKPOINT. Pause before acting.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A3.F7.pic2.2.2" class="ltx_p" style="width:471.0pt;"><span id="A3.F7.pic2.2.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:80%;width:471.0pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A3.F7.pic2.2.2.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:471.0pt;">
<span id="A3.F7.pic2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.F7.pic2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Answer these three questions in at most 60 words total:</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A3.F7.pic2.2.3" class="ltx_p" style="width:471.0pt;"><span id="A3.F7.pic2.2.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:80%;width:471.0pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A3.F7.pic2.2.3.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:471.0pt;">
<span id="A3.F7.pic2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.F7.pic2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">  1. What is the current state of the task, and what have your recent actions actually changed?</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A3.F7.pic2.2.4" class="ltx_p" style="width:471.0pt;"><span id="A3.F7.pic2.2.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:80%;width:471.0pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A3.F7.pic2.2.4.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:471.0pt;">
<span id="A3.F7.pic2.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.F7.pic2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">  2. Can the approach you are currently using complete this task, or has it stalled?</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A3.F7.pic2.2.5" class="ltx_p" style="width:471.0pt;"><span id="A3.F7.pic2.2.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:80%;width:471.0pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A3.F7.pic2.2.5.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:471.0pt;">
<span id="A3.F7.pic2.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.F7.pic2.p5.1" class="ltx_p">  3. If it can, say so and continue with it. If it cannot, say what you will do differently.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A3.F7.pic2.2.6" class="ltx_p" style="width:471.0pt;"><span id="A3.F7.pic2.2.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:80%;width:471.0pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A3.F7.pic2.2.6.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:471.0pt;">
<span id="A3.F7.pic2.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.F7.pic2.p6.1" class="ltx_p">Then take your next action.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span></div></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A3.F7.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 7</span>: </span><span id="A3.F7.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Handoff and checkpoint prompts. Handoff retains up to six recent weak-agent steps by default; bracketed screenshot markers indicate image inputs, not literal prompt text. The neutral checkpoint requests reassessment without asserting that execution has stalled and explicitly permits continuing the current approach.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Execution context.</h4>

<div id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The inherited OSWorld system prompt mentions shell and editor tools, although this harness exposes only the <span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">computer</span> tool. A system suffix corrects the sudo password for the Docker environment. The diagnostic state query is logging-only, and the alternative <span id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">think_reflect</span> prompt is not used by the hidden-state checkpoint.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A4" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix D </span>Case Study</h2>

<section id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Runtime escalation case studies.</h4>

<div id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#A4.F8" title="Figure 8 ‣ Runtime escalation case studies. ‣ Appendix D Case Study ‣ LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>–<a href="#A4.F10" title="Figure 10 ‣ Runtime escalation case studies. ‣ Appendix D Case Study ‣ LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a> present three representative examples of runtime escalation. Across all three cases, the weak agent remains on an unproductive GUI-based trajectory before the runtime gate triggers handoff. After takeover, the strong agent changes the execution strategy rather than simply continuing the weak agent’s actions <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">Song et al., 2026</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">In the first case, the weak agent repeatedly interacts with an unresponsive macro interface while attempting to standardize text-box fonts. <em id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">LEASH</em> hands off at step 11, after which the strong agent switches from the macro GUI to a terminal-based <span id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">python-pptx</span> solution and completes the task in 27 actions; the Manager-only run instead exhausts the 50-action budget.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">In the second case, the weak agent repeatedly opens, inspects, and closes candidate photos. Handoff occurs at step 8, and the strong agent replaces this loop with keyboard navigation and multi-selection, successfully creating the requested archive in 27 actions. The corresponding Manager-only run creates an incorrect archive and receives a score of zero.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">In the third case, the weak agent spends 23 steps browsing and searching without installing the requested LibreOffice extension. After handoff at step 24, the strong agent switches to a terminal-based installation strategy and successfully installs LanguageTool, whereas the Manager-only run exhausts the action budget without completing the installation.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Together, these examples illustrate that runtime escalation can identify stalled or inefficient execution trajectories and enable a strong agent to adopt qualitatively different strategies rather than merely continuing the weak agent’s current path.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A4.F8" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2610.22280v1/x1.png" id="A4.F8.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:429/157;" width="429" height="157" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A4.F8.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 8</span>: </span><span id="A4.F8.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Runtime escalation case study I: font standardization.<span id="A4.F8.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> The weak agent becomes stuck in repeated macro-interface interactions. After handoff at step 11, the strong agent switches to a terminal-based <span id="A4.F8.6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">python-pptx</span> strategy and successfully completes the task.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="A4.F9" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2610.22280v1/x2.png" id="A4.F9.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:429/156;" width="429" height="156" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A4.F9.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 9</span>: </span><span id="A4.F9.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Runtime escalation case study II: photo selection.<span id="A4.F9.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> The weak agent enters a repeated open–inspect–close loop. After handoff at step 8, the strong agent changes to keyboard navigation and multi-selection and successfully creates the requested archive.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="A4.F10" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2610.22280v1/x3.png" id="A4.F10.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:429/146;" width="429" height="146" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A4.F10.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 10</span>: </span><span id="A4.F10.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Runtime escalation case study III: extension installation.<span id="A4.F10.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> The weak agent continues browsing without completing the installation. After handoff at step 24, the strong agent switches to a terminal-based installation strategy and successfully installs the requested extension.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
</section>
